name: Apache Cassandra
tagline: Masterless wide-column database built for always-on writes across data centers.
description: Cassandra is the Dynamo-meets-Bigtable database: a ring of equal nodes, tunable consistency per query, and an LSM storage engine that soaks up enormous write volumes without a single point of failure. It is the default open-source choice when you need multi-datacenter replication and linear write scaling, and it powers some of the largest deployments on the planet. Version 5.0 added Storage-Attached Indexes, vector search and the Unified Compaction Strategy; the 6.0 line (in alpha) brings Accord general-purpose ACID transactions. Expect to model tables per query and to invest in operations (repair, compaction, JVM tuning).

pricing.notes: Free to self-host; managed Cassandra from DataStax (IBM), AWS Keyspaces, Azure and Instaclustr.

managedServices.name: Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra

scale.notes: Consistent hashing with vnodes; clusters of hundreds to thousands of nodes and multi-PB datasets are documented (Apple, Netflix).

strengths: No single point of failure: every node accepts reads and writes
Multi-datacenter replication with per-query consistency levels (LOCAL_QUORUM, EACH_QUORUM)
LSM write path absorbs very high sustained write throughput
Storage-Attached Indexes and native vector search since 5.0
Vendor-neutral Apache project with a large managed-service ecosystem
weaknesses: Query-first data modelling; no joins and limited ad-hoc filtering
Lightweight transactions (Paxos) are slow; full ACID transactions are still in the 6.0 alpha
Operational load: repairs, compaction tuning, tombstones and JVM GC
Read latency tails can suffer under heavy compaction or wide partitions
useCases: Fraud and personalisation features served at scale
notIdealFor: Relational workloads needing joins or multi-row ACID
Small datasets that fit one Postgres node
Teams without operational capacity for repairs and tuning
